settings.title: Settings
settings.devices.note: Detected means the driver reports the device. Tested means a model has recorded evidence on it. One does not imply the other.
settings.language.note: Applies immediately and is remembered in this workspace. Interface text and generated explanations follow this language; original technical records retain their source text.

gallery.body: Every domain component rendered on fixed mock fixtures generated from the contract examples. Nothing here is a computed result.
gallery.perf: Performance probe: PSD with {psd} points × {traces} traces and an I/Q window of {iq} samples rendered in {ms} ms.

datasets.import.title: Import my data
datasets.import.upload.help: CSV, .npy or .npz up to 2 GB; it is stored under the workspace imports folder and never anywhere else.
datasets.import.noFiles: No CSV / .npy / .npz files here. Copy files into the import root or upload one.
datasets.import.mapping.help: Which column holds each logical signal. Guessed from the headers; fix any mistake here, including swapped I/Q.
datasets.import.signal.help: Needed by the evaluation profile; without them formal metrics are blocked, not guessed.
datasets.import.name: Display name
datasets.detail.versions.empty: Only raw-v1 (built-in datasets keep their original split).
datasets.detail.doctor.empty: No report yet. The doctor checks NaN/Inf, length, outliers, clipping plateaus, delay, gain, amplitude, bandwidth and metadata, and says which evaluations would be unreliable.
datasets.detail.doctor.blocked: Formal evaluation is blocked until the error items are resolved.
datasets.preprocess.title: Preprocess (creates a new version)
datasets.preprocess.help: Raw files are never modified. Preview first; a version is written only when you confirm. Normalisation is fitted on the training split only.
datasets.preprocess.normalize: Normalise by the training-split input peak
datasets.import.pick: Pick a file on the left (or upload one) to inspect it.
datasets.preprocess.version.help: Letters, digits, dots, dashes; e.g. aligned-v1. Cannot overwrite an existing version.
results.detail.profile.help: Every registered profile is scored from the same best checkpoint; the configured one is the primary result.
results.detail.definitions.help: What each score means under {profile} v{version}. Names, formulas and better-directions come from the registry, not from the page.
form.profile.help: The definition behind every score of the result. Every registered profile is also stored; this one is shown first.
form.import.help: A JSON experiment configuration (exported from a run or written by hand). It is validated by the server and submitted as is.
form.imported: Imported configuration from {source}. The server validates and runs the configuration shown below. You can change the optional name; discard the import to use the recipe form.
run.lineage.help: Read from resolved configurations: which checkpoints this run used and which runs used it.
run.lineage.empty: This run neither uses nor is used by another run.
run.apply: Apply DPD to the test split…
run.apply.title: Apply this DPD to the test split
run.apply.help: Exports u = DPD(x), the pre-distorted PA input, and scores y = PA(u) through the chosen surrogate against the same linear target as the training result. The export is a PA input, not a PA output, and does not by itself show linearisation.
run.apply.surrogate.help: Another succeeded PA run of the same dataset gives a new, separately stored result; the DPD's own result is never overwritten.
run.measure.title: Score captures of a physical PA driven by this export
run.measure.help: You played this run's exported u = DPD(x) (and, under the same conditions, x itself) through a PA and captured the output with an I/Q analyser. Upload the capture files and declare the set-up. OpenDPD aligns each capture to what was played (integer delay, one complex gain), scores it as captured under every profile and stores the captures with their hashes.
run.measure.attestation: The result will be labelled as a user-provided measurement, not independently verified by OpenDPD. Keep the output power, waveform and operating point identical between the two captures; any level difference is reported, never normalised away.
run.measure.with.help: PA output while u = DPD(x) was played (.csv with I/Q columns, .npy (n, 2) or .npz). Required.
run.measure.without.help: PA output while x was played directly, same conditions. Optional; it becomes the measured baseline.
run.measure.drive.help: Generator level and PA input drive as set
run.measure.chain.help: Generator → PA → attenuation → analyser, as wired, with instrument identities
run.measure.rate.help: Rate of the capture files; the dataset rate is prefilled
run.measure.playback.help: Looped playback lets the aligned window wrap around the file
results.detail.chain.help: x is the target input, u = DPD(x) the pre-distorted PA input, y the PA output. A simulated stage comes from a learned surrogate, never from a measurement.
results.detail.baselines.help: Every column is scored against the same linear target reference_gain · x, with the same profile and valid range. Nothing is normalised separately, so power differences stay visible.
results.detail.measurement.level: Output level with DPD relative to without: {db} dB (capture units).
results.detail.measurement.level.warn: The captures are not at the same output level, so their difference is not attributable to the DPD alone.
results.detail.coverage.body: Largest fitted |x| {fitted} · peak |u| {peak} · {fraction} of the pre-distorted samples above the fitted peak.
results.detail.scaling.body: Amplitude units: {units} · input scaling: {scaling} · reference gain: {gain}.
results.detail.scaling.uncalibrated: No physical calibration: absolute output power (dBm) and efficiency are not derived from these numbers.
run.metrics.fitted: This run finished without per-epoch metrics: the model was fitted in one step (a least-squares baseline). Open the result for its scores and the fit record.
run.metrics.apply: This run scored stored weights (a DPD applied to the test split, a PA model on another condition, or measured captures); there is no training history. Open the result for the signal chain and the scores.
results.charts.help: Drawn from plots-v1 data the worker computed from the evaluated arrays (the spectral profile's Welch estimator). Hiding a trace in the legend changes nothing in the evaluation.
results.charts.none: No derived plot data for this result (it was evaluated before plots-v1). Re-evaluate the run to produce it.
chart.am.title: AM-AM
chart.pm.title: AM-PM
compare.title: Compare results
compare.pick: Pick at least two results on the Results page to compare them.
compare.comparable: Same protocol: these results may be ranked; the best value per metric is marked.
compare.incompatible: Different protocols: the results are shown side by side and are not ranked.
compare.spectrum: Spectrum overlay (primary trace of each result)
compare.spectrum.mismatch: The results were evaluated on different frequency axes; no overlay is drawn.
run.metrics.fromHistory: Curves come from the run's history log.
results.export.help: A package carries the resolved configuration, the results under every profile, the plot data, the checkpoints of every referenced run, the reports and the commands to reproduce. Full is private and complete; share leaves your PA data, worker logs and machine paths out and says so.
experiments.import.help: An experiment package exported by OpenDPD Studio (.zip). Every file hash is verified before anything is written; a damaged or unsupported package is refused with the reason.
logs.capped: Only the last {max} lines are kept in the viewer; older lines are in the downloadable log.
robustness.title: Robustness across conditions
robustness.intro: Adaptation reports under the conditions-v1 protocol: one device, one varied dimension, every cell of the matrix kept (failures included). Reports are built from the command line and read here; nothing is recomputed.
robustness.empty: No adaptation report in this workspace yet. Register a plan and build one with `opendpd adaptation plan … && opendpd adaptation run … && opendpd adaptation report …`.
robustness.list.label: Adaptation reports
robustness.bar.detail: {n} conditions (bar {min}); independent capture batches: {independent}; measured origin: {measured}
robustness.bar.rehearsal: Below the evidence bar: this report is a rehearsal of the protocol, not evidence.
robustness.matrix.label: Condition matrix
robustness.cost.label: Cost of adaptation
run.stream.help: Runs this run's weights as {variant}: the state is carried across chunks instead of being reset at every segment. A separate result that is never compared with the offline score.
results.detail.execution.consistent: Chunk consistency: streamed in chunks of {chunk} samples, the outputs match the full-sequence run of the same variant within {tolerance} (max error {error}).
results.detail.execution.inconsistent: Chunk consistency FAILED: streamed in chunks of {chunk} samples, the outputs differ from the full-sequence run by up to {error} (tolerance {tolerance}); the numbers depend on the chunking.
results.detail.execution.note: Look-ahead is the future an output needs (an information bound), not the measured latency of an implementation. The tail is zero-padded at flush.
results.deploy.help: A fixed-point-v1 package: quantised weights, six golden vectors with the state after every sample, a C99 reference verified bit for bit against the software reference, and a report whose numbers say how they were obtained (theoretical, measured execution time, synthesis estimate, measured power). One model, one precision scheme; the rules are pending a maintainer's approval.
results.deploy.unsupported: No fixed-point specification for {model}. fixed-point-v1 covers {supported} (one layer, executed as gru_stream); other models have no deployment export yet.
results.deploy.building: Quantising, replaying golden vectors, compiling the C reference…
results.deploy.verification.bit_exact: Bit-exact: {backend} reference verified on {cases} golden vectors.
results.deploy.verification.mismatch: Mismatch: the {backend} reference differs from the software reference.
results.deploy.verification.not_run: Not verified: the {backend} sources were generated but no C compiler ran them.
results.deploy.mismatch: First difference in case {case} at sample {step}, signal {signal}.
results.deploy.resources: {mac} MAC per sample, {lookups} table lookups per sample; weights {weights} B, state {state} B, tables {tables} B; no sparsity exploited
results.deploy.measured: {rate} samples/s: {what}. A property of this build on this machine, not of a deployment.
results.deploy.notMeasuredPower: not available: nothing was measured; energy is never inferred from MAC or parameter counts
inspection.constellationNote: Dataset-specific demodulation. Output uses input-referenced equalization; the plot is not a standard EVM measurement.
inspection.iqNote: Sampled baseband I/Q, not demodulated symbol constellations. Known reference symbols and a receiver are required for symbol EVM.
inspection.measurementNote: ACPR: negative dBc, lower is better. Hover or focus a value for its measurement conditions.
inspection.noPlots: Charts require finite, paired I/Q samples. Check Dataset Doctor for details.
inspection.window: Capture window {start}–{end} / {total} samples · charts are subsampled; metrics use the full analysis window.
datasets.builtin.title: Built-in datasets
datasets.builtin.help: Choose any dataset shipped with this OpenDPD installation. Adding one copies it into the current workspace.
datasets.create.title: Create Your Own Dataset
datasets.create.help: One row is one paired PA input/output sample, in capture time order. Choose either of these layouts.
datasets.create.formatHelp: Comma-separated UTF-8; optional unique headers. Complex cells accept i or j and scientific notation. The examples show the format only; provide a complete capture.
datasets.create.csvOnly: Choose a .csv file. Export spreadsheets as CSV UTF-8 (comma delimited).
datasets.create.valid: All {count} sample rows passed. Confirm the input/output column roles before continuing.
datasets.create.splitHelp: Keep samples in time order. Percentages apply after two boundary guards are excluded; the shared split protocol calculates the exact counts.
datasets.create.numbers: Enter three positive percentages and a non-negative whole number for the guard.
datasets.create.guardHelp: Default: {count} samples at each boundary. Guards isolate overlapping training frames; keep them at least as long as your frame length.
datasets.create.idHelp: 1–64 characters: letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores; start with a letter or digit.
datasets.create.signalHelp: Enter known physical values only. Without a sample rate, the spectrum uses normalized frequency. Imported CSVs show raw I/Q unless a receiver/reference waveform is bound.
datasets.create.signalInvalid: Use positive finite numbers; carrier count and FFT length must be whole numbers.
datasets.create.ready: Validated {count} paired samples. Review the split before creating the dataset.
datasets.create.guardReview: {count} guard samples at each boundary ({total} excluded from training/validation/test). Raw samples remain intact.
datasets.create.afterCreate: The original CSV is preserved with its hash. Next, inspect the signal, add any missing metadata, then configure an experiment.
datasets.create.fixSamples: Use finite, non-empty decimal or scientific numbers within the float32 range. Complex cells accept a+bj or a+bi. Correct the paired source sample; do not leave blanks, NaN or infinity.
datasets.create.fixFormat: Export a UTF-8 comma-delimited CSV with two complex or four real columns. Check quotes, separators and file availability.
datasets.create.fixRow: Make every row contain exactly the selected number of fields. Restore missing samples, remove extra separators and blank lines, and keep input/output pairs aligned.
datasets.create.fixMapping: Use unique non-empty column names and assign each input/output role to a different column. Set the first row correctly as header or data.
datasets.create.fixSplit: Enter three positive percentages summing to 100%. Supply enough data for non-empty splits and both guards; choose guards that isolate your training frames.
datasets.create.fixEmpty: Add a complete paired input/output capture below the optional header. The file needs more than headers or a format illustration.

tasks.startingSettings.help: Choose a starting point, then adjust the hyperparameters in the next step.
tasks.threads.help: Leave empty to use the runtime default.
testing.model.help: Choose a successfully completed training run.
testing.model.none: Train a model first, then return here to test it.
testing.surrogate.help: Use the PA model used during DPD training, or another trained PA model on this dataset.
testing.trainingSurrogate: PA model used during DPD training
testing.frozen: The trained weights, architecture and frame settings are reused. Choose how to execute and score the test below.
testing.execution.help: Streaming is offered only when a compatible implementation exists for these weights.

guide.title: Create your first dataset
guide.intro: We’ll walk through the actual setup together. Use your CSV, or try a built-in dataset if you don’t have one yet.
guide.file: Choose the file and check the input/output columns.
guide.split: Set the train, validation and test proportions.
guide.review: Review the sample counts, then create the dataset.
guide.ready.title: Your dataset is ready to inspect
guide.ready.body: Inspect the signals and metadata on this page. The checks explain anything missing. Once it is ready for training, use Configure experiment to continue.
guide.builtin.help: Choose any dataset to try. MyCustomPA is synthetic tutorial data. Add opens it for inspection; it does not start training.
guide.csv.file: Step 1 · Upload a CSV with paired input/output samples. We check every row and help you fix any format problems before continuing.
guide.csv.split: Step 2 · Keep the suggested split or adjust it. Give the dataset a name. Signal metadata can be added here or later.
guide.csv.review: Step 3 · Check the final sample counts. Create dataset saves it and opens the signal inspection page.
chart.controls.summary: Two fingers: pan · Pinch or Ctrl/Cmd + wheel: zoom · Double-click: fit
chart.controls.pan: Pan: move two fingers on a trackpad, scroll the wheel, or drag the plot. Shift + wheel pans horizontally.
chart.controls.zoom: Zoom: pinch on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl/Cmd while scrolling. Zoom follows the pointer.
chart.controls.mouse: Mouse: select the zoom tool for box zoom and direct wheel zoom. The mode bar also has zoom and fit buttons.
chart.controls.keyboard: Keyboard: focus the plot, then use arrows to pan, + / − to zoom, Home or 0 to fit, P to pan, and Z to select zoom.
chart.controls.page: Page scrolling: scroll outside the plotting area, or hold Alt while scrolling over a plot.
terminal.independent: These tabs switch logs only; your experiment page stays where it is.
terminal.empty: No run in this step yet. Its terminal will appear when you start an experiment.
live.title: Live experiment
live.geometry: {samples} complex I/Q samples per batch @ {rate} · each sample contains I and Q
live.stride: Frame stride {stride} samples; overlapping samples count again
live.waitingGeometry: Waiting for the worker to build the data loaders…
live.cadence: Signal preview: at least {batches} batches and {seconds} s between updates; adapts to model cost. First batch is shown immediately.
live.surrogate: DPD output is evaluated through the trained PA surrogate. These plots show the simulated signal chain.
live.finalHelp: Stored test-split plots from the evaluated checkpoint and the shared metric service.
live.probeHelp: Fixed {source} segment · {samples} I/Q samples. Preview metrics are diagnostic; checkpoint selection uses the original full validation pass.
live.waitingSignals: The first computed signal preview will appear here.
live.unavailable: The live snapshot could not be loaded. Progress and terminal logs remain available.
about.title: About
about.description: An open framework for power amplifier modelling and digital predistortion. Developed by the Lab of Efficient Machine Intelligence, Delft University of Technology.
about.refreshNote: Checks GitHub every five minutes while this page is open. Contribution totals may be cached by GitHub. Last successful check
about.offline: GitHub is currently unavailable. Any displayed activity is the last successful snapshot; repository links still work.
live.padding: Includes {count} zero-padding samples in the final evaluation sequence.

web.retention: Temporary workspace · download your results before {date}. Files are deleted automatically.

web.connection.hint: Check your network connection and retry. If the domain was recently moved, your network may still have old DNS records; try another network or a trusted DNS resolver.
terminal.readOnly: Read-only output. Use Stop experiment to terminate this run.
run.gpuQueue: The shared GPU runs one experiment at a time. Your experiment is queued; you can leave this page and return to it.
chart.controls.touch: Two fingers: zoom and pan. One finger: scroll the page.
datasets.upload.limit: CSV only: UTF-8, at most 25 MiB and 1,000,000 paired samples.
datasets.upload.checking: Validating file type and every CSV row before preview…
model.download.help: Weights selected by the best validation score so far. Save them before the workspace expires.
model.download.waiting: Available after the first model checkpoint is saved.
model.download.error: Could not check model availability. Retry shortly.
